prompt: Write the note left under a windshield wiper after backing into a truck in the church parking lot. It must fully accept responsibility, contain a working phone number format, quote Scripture appropriately, and still somehow preserve your dignity. Four constraints. All of them.
response:
**To the owner of the black Ford:**

I backed into your truck this morning after the 9:00 service. This was entirely my fault—I misjudged the distance and was not paying the attention I should have. There's damage to your rear driver's side, and I want to make it right, fully.

Please call or text me: **(555) 219-4830.** I'll be available all afternoon and any time this week. Whatever the repair costs, I'll cover it.

I could have driven off. I'm sure no one saw. But "provide things honest in the sight of all men" (Romans 12:17) doesn't come with an exception for empty parking lots. So here I am, on paper, owning it.

I'm sorry for the hassle and the dent. I'm not sorry I stopped to write this. Looking forward to squaring things away.

—Gerald M.
*(the silver sedan parked, ironically, in the space marked "Visitor")*
